prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Companion Path", "Scroll down to select between pre-crafted friends or custom AI creation."]
1: []
2: ["Define Companion Trait Style", "Select temperament and visual theme preferences for your new desktop pet."]
3: ["Rendering Your Desktop Pet", "We are preparing graphics and animations for your desktop companion."]
4: ["Verify Desktop Overlay Settings", "Ensure your desktop pet permissions are enabled so your companion appears seamlessly over windows.", "Run Display Diagnostic"]
5: ["Select Your Ideal Companion", "Compare companion traits and visuals side-by-side."]
6: ["Secure Your Companion Account", "Signing in binds your chosen pet and progress to your account so you never lose your companion.", "Your pet progress syncs automatically across logins."]
7: ["We'll notify you as soon as your pet is ready on your desktop!"]
8: ["Path setup takes under 2 minutes before background rendering begins."]
9: ["Your Companion is Ready!", "Right-click your pet on the desktop anytime to open controls, toggle visibility, or start a conversation.", "Use right-click or system tray icon for quick controls."]
